report:
Fresh source assessment of meta.anchors.book_explorer using the current start inputs and captured dependencies. No test suite or browser was run in this review; centralized execution is separate evidence. No source changes were made.

Requirements and implementation: (1) The book must include the explorer, model and Rust snapshots. The ordinary book.rs association covers preprocess/generate_crates, which load the configured Crates model, validate it and its correspondence, generate chapters and write sage-explorer.html into the source tree for mdBook copying. The ordinary browser.rs association covers render_book_browser and render: the same Document representation is serialized alongside indexed Rust source text and locations, with JavaScript and CSS embedded inline. (2) Explorer chapters must embed the browser and offer full-page viewing. chapter/explorer_frame produce a depth-relative iframe URL with embed and route parameters and a full-page anchor with encoded route. (3) The handwritten Crates landing page must link to searchable/interlinked Sage chapters. The actual captured README has subsystem links; generation preserves landing content and adds crate/module children. browser.js builds scoped model maps, supplies links for modeled declarations and members and in-memory search/filtering, with source-pane controls wired by index.html. (4) Book and local serving must share the model/renderer: captured main.rs loads Document values and calls render_browser_with_workspace before server::serve; that function and render_book_browser both call render. (5) Published browsing, including Rust source, must work without sage-meta serve. The browser reads embedded model-data/source-data, and renderSourcePane uses sources.files and indexed locations directly, rather than a server fetch. Embedded navigation can fall back to independent hash navigation if parent access is denied; source absence is explicitly rendered. (6) Rebuilds must refresh both model and Rust source. workspace::load_documents rereads Sage files; render calls source_data, which constructs a new CorrespondenceIndex; captured load/load_file initialize fresh state and read Rust files. Changed serialized HTML replaces the asset; identical content avoids a write. The snapshot labels in the frame, template and source pane explain the captured nature of those values.

Complete test set: book_asset_is_self_contained_and_embeds_exact_script_safe_model_and_source checks no external script/stylesheet dependency, no remaining template placeholders, script-safe serialization, exact recovered model prose and Rust text, indexed correspondence identity and nested chapter paths. curated_crates_landing_preserves_prose_and_links_to_generated_chapters checks exact retained prose after source-link rewriting, retained entity fragments, no replacement iframe, generated crate/module nesting, companion links and home metadata. generates_crate_and_module_chapters_for_both_mdbook_protocols checks both items and sections protocols, chapter hierarchy/paths, iframe and full-page controls, the relative asset link, model descriptions and asset existence. unchanged_preprocessing_preserves_asset_timestamp_and_source_edits_refresh_it checks byte/timestamp stability when unchanged and refreshed model prose in both asset and chapter after editing. These are meaningful assertions visible in the annotated test bodies. The captured Fixture invokes the actual preprocessor in an isolated workspace; chapters traverses output and script_data parses the embedded JSON.

The remaining todo::self_contained_book_explorer has no executable assertions and is assessed only as explicit deferred coverage. Its comment requests building and browsing the embedded/full-page explorer with Rust source without a Sage server and refreshing after source changes. Structural output, source embedding and model regeneration are tested above, but this anchor's associated tests do not drive a real browser or a Rust-only edit/rebuild lifecycle. That TODO honestly retains the remaining integration gap: completion requires a built-book browser fixture, interaction with search/entity links and Rust source in both presentations while no Sage server runs, and checks that model and Rust edits appear after rebuild. It is not counted as a successful browser test or relabeled implemented. No N/A entries exist. The source inspection found no concrete behavior contradicting this delivery claim. All implementation entries and four ordinary plus one TODO test entries are accounted for; the justified TODO remains visible. No edits are requested.
